novelty.justification: The core mechanism extends prior model-based performance prediction and statistical detection work by propagating distributions instead of point estimates, fixing the stated limitation that 'point propagation ignores noise; subjective statistical thresholds'. This is a meaningful extension rather than a new paradigm, since stochastic/queueing and statistical detection approaches already exist in the Solution Space.
novelty.rubric: Incremental: a meaningful extension or optimization of prior baseline work that fixes a concrete prior limitation, but the core paradigm is unchanged.
novelty.differentiation: Relative to model-based performance prediction and statistical regression-detection work, the proposed addition is explicit distributional propagation from component-level tests through an architectural/queueing model with calibrated alarm thresholds, rather than point estimates or purely learned surrogate detection.

feasibility.justification: The plan requires re-implementing a point-propagation baseline and a distributional propagation method, obtaining or building a queueing model for TeaStore, and
feasibility.rubric: Moderate workload (sweet spot): needs nontrivial coding such as scripting existing open-source tools (parsers, CFG extractors) or building a custom graph-processing pipeline; standard research engineering effort.

original.paper_title: Early Detection of Performance Regressions by Bridging Local Performance Data and Architectural Models

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: The proposed approach can effectively detect end-to-end system performance regressions from local performance deviations with different intensities.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can effectively detect system performance regressions with different intensities of local performance deviations

claims.statement: The proposed approach can detect regressions as early as the development phase, before full system performance testing is available.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can detect regressions as early as in the development phase, in contrast to existing approaches that require the system to be fully built and deployed

claims.statement: Significant local performance deviations do not always cause system-level performance regressions, and the approach avoids false alarms in fixed-workload cases without system regressions.
claims.evidence_quote: Our approach does not generate false alarms when there is local performance deviation but no system performance regression.

claims.statement: Under various workloads, the approach maintains effectiveness: TeaStore is consistent with system testing in seven out of nine cases, and TrainTicket model predictions align except for an undetectable L1 case.
claims.evidence_quote: for TeaStore, our approach maintains consistency with the performance testing results in seven out of nine cases

original.overall_conclusion: The proposed approach bridges component-level performance deviation detection and architectural models to infer system-level performance regressions early in the development phase. Across TeaStore and TrainTicket benchmarks, fixed-workload evaluations show that the approach detects most injected regressions while avoiding false alarms in no-regression cases, and various-workload evaluations show maintained consistency in most cases.
original.comparable_notes: The comparison uses open-source systems TeaStore and TrainTicket, injected regressions at L1-L3, Low/Medium/High intensities, component-level tests repeated 30 times, system performance tests run 15 minutes with 5-minute warm-up and repeated 3 times, and regression outcomes derived from response time effect size and CPU MPD differences.

claims.statement: The proposed method retains the full empirical distribution of component-level timing deviations and propagates it through a queueing-network architectural model via Monte Carlo sampling.
claims.evidence_quote: retain the full empirical distribution of component-level timing deviations, propagate it through a queueing-network architectural model via Monte Carlo sampling

claims.statement: The method issues a regression alarm using a calibrated probability rule P(delta RT > theta) >= beta.
claims.evidence_quote: issue a regression alarm with a calibrated probability rule (`P(ΔRT > θ) ≥ β`)

claims.statement: On TeaStore with regressions injected at three architectural locations and three intensities, the approach recovers the per-request regression magnitude with a mean absolute error of 0.175 ms.
claims.evidence_quote: recovers the per-request regression magnitude with a mean absolute error of 0.175 ms

claims.statement: The approach detects all nine injected regressions with near-perfect accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: detects all nine regressions with near-perfect accuracy

claims.statement: The 90% predictive interval covers the ground-truth response-time change in 9 out of 9 scenarios.
claims.evidence_quote: its 90% predictive interval covers the ground-truth response-time change in 9/9 scenarios

claims.statement: Workload amplifies regression impact and ultimately drives saturation.
claims.evidence_quote: reveals how workload amplifies regression impact and ultimately drives saturation

claims.statement: The distributional formulation contributes uncertainty quantification, predictive intervals, and calibrated alarms that deterministic point propagation cannot provide.
claims.evidence_quote: The distributional formulation contributes uncertainty quantification—predictive intervals and calibrated alarms—that deterministic point propagation cannot provide

claims.statement: Point and distributional propagation are statistically indistinguishable on raw detection rate at the clean separations studied.
claims.evidence_quote: point and distributional propagation are statistically indistinguishable on raw detection rate

agent.overall_conclusion: The distributional architectural propagation method recovers per-request regression magnitude with a mean absolute error of 0.175 ms, detects all nine injected TeaStore regressions, and provides calibrated 90% predictive intervals with 9/9 coverage. Its main contribution is uncertainty quantification beyond deterministic point propagation, while raw detection rate is equivalent to point propagation at the clean separations studied.

claim_alignment.label: consistent
claim_alignment.rationale: Both assert improved detection of system-level or end-to-end regressions from local/component-level deviations; agent reports all nine TeaStore injected regressions detected, matching the improvement direction.

claim_alignment.label: missing
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent describes propagation from component-level deviations to a queueing-network model but does not explicitly evaluate or claim detection as early as the development phase before full system testing.

claim_alignment.label: missing
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent does not report false-alarm avoidance on fixed-workload no-regression cases or cases with local deviations but no system regression.

claim_alignment.label: missing

metric_alignment.rationale: Original reports a TeaStore fixed-workload L1 Low response-time testing MPD; agent reports mean absolute error of per-request regression magnitude across three locations/intensities, not the same protocol or metric.
Original model-prediction MPD is not reported by agent; agent's 0.175 ms MAE is a different quantity and setting.
Agent does not report CPU MPD for TeaStore fixed workload.
Agent does not report CPU model-prediction MPD for TeaStore fixed workload.

summary.score_rationale: The agent works on the same research direction of inferring system-level regression from local/component-level deviations and agrees on the main detection claim, but it does not address early-development, false-alarm, or various-workload consistency claims and reports non-comparable evaluation metrics.

experiment_success.note: success=true requires substantive results (framework-aware path) with >=3 numeric leaves. Supports metrics.json, results.json, experiment_results.txt, etc. Manifest returncode/benchmark_complete are soft warnings only.

idea_code_consistency.label: severe_mismatch
idea_code_consistency.justification: The provided code consists only of a few TeaStore entity classes (Category, ImageSize, ImageSizePreset, Order). These are ordinary domain model classes with getters/setters and equals/hashCode, completely unrelated to the research idea of uncertainty-aware early performance-regression detection via distributional architectural propagation. There is no implementation of point-propagation baseline, distributional propagation, calibrated alarms, TPR/FPR metrics, or any evaluation protocol. The code is boilerplate application code, not an experiment implementing the stated idea.
matched_elements: Presence of Java classes from the TeaStore domain (but not specific to the research idea)
missing_or_divergent_elements: Uncertainty-aware regression detection with calibrated alarms
Evaluation protocol (component tests, queueing model, Monte Carlo, embedded-Tomcat+JMeter oracle)
Any experiment entrypoint or runnable pipeline
idea_code_consistency.rubric: Severe mismatch: code implements a different problem/method than the idea, or is unrelated boilerplate.

components.significance_evidence: stats.py artifact exists with Wilcoxon signal, but final metrics.json is empty and no executed p-value/CI/bootstrap result is reported.

components.name: Calibrated alarm rule P(ΔRT > θ) ≥ β
components.ablation_evidence: No controlled comparison removing or varying the calibrated alarm rule is described in the evidence.
components.significance_evidence: Descriptive component; no separate statistical test required.

components.name: Point-propagation baseline
components.ablation_evidence: Baseline is the comparison target, not a removable method component.
components.significance_evidence: Same stats.py/Wilcoxon artifact exists, but no formal statistical comparison result is reported between the two methods.

components.name: TeaStore benchmark with injected regressions
components.ablation_evidence: Benchmark setup, not a removable method component.
components.significance_evidence: Descriptive benchmark coverage; no formal test expected.

ablation_significance.summary: This is a new-method study with a point-propagation baseline. The core distributional-propagation module has a baseline comparison as an ablation, but the calibrated alarm rule lacks an explicit controlled ablation. Significance tests are indicated by a stats.py artifact with Wilcoxon signals, but no executed p-values, CIs, or bootstrap results are reported in the metrics evidence, so significance is only partially supported.
